sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim (Site 04)
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: A prominent Artemis candidate region on the elevated rim of Shackleton Crater (-89.9°S). Features near-permanent illumination on high peaks alongside deep permanent shadow within the crater interior.

provenance.note: Representative point on the Shackleton crater ridge derived from NASA GSFC PGDA high-resolution LOLA polar products.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge (Site 01)
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: Connecting Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. One of NASA's highest-priority Artemis III exploration zones, offering strategic illumination windows and cross-crater line-of-sight.

provenance.note: Candidate region representative point derived from NASA PGDA Site01 LOLA elevation data.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (Site 23)
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: Massive 5,000 m mountain massif near the south pole. Outstanding line-of-sight directly towards Earth provides nearly continuous geometric communications visibility, combined with high solar illumination.

provenance.note: Representative point on Malapert Massif peak derived from NASA PGDA Site23 elevation dataset.

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton (Site 07)
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: Elevated topographic high near Shackleton with high percentage solar availability during lunar summer, situated on the edge of the South Pole-Aitken basin.

provenance.note: Representative location derived from NASA GSFC PGDA Site07 5m/pixel polar stereographic product.

sites.name: Amundsen–Ritchie Rim
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: A rugged south-polar candidate region on the rim of Amundsen crater with complex topographic shadow casting and intermittent Earth visibility.

provenance.note: Regional representative point derived from NASA PDS LOLA polar GDR DEM products.

sites.name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: Historic Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage in Mare Tranquillitatis. Serves as an equatorial low-relief reference where the Sun rises and sets on an exact 29.5-day cycle with Earth high overhead.

provenance.note: Published NASA NSSDCA Apollo landing site coordinates in planetocentric DE421/DE440 Mean Earth frame.

sites.name: Apollo 17 Taurus-Littrow
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: Apollo 17 valley site bounded by steep massifs rising 1.5–2 km above the valley floor. Demonstrates how severe valley terrain blocks sunlight and low-elevation lines of sight.

provenance.note: Published NASA NSSDCA Apollo 17 landing coordinates in Taurus-Littrow Valley.

sites.name: Sinus Medii (Equatorial Reference)
sites.elevation_datum: radial height above NAIF BODY301_RADII mean sphere (1737.4 km)
sites.description: The intersection of the Lunar Equator and Prime Meridian (0°N, 0°E). Ideal mathematical and physical reference where Earth is permanently located directly at the zenith (90° elevation).

provenance.note: Zero-point coordinate definition for Mean Earth / Polar Axis frame with flat mathematical horizon.
